metadata.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptive Lane Detection via Contextual Contrast and Aggregation

section.title: Abstract and Introduction
section.summary: The paper addresses unsupervised domain adaptive lane detection, focusing on discriminative feature learning and cross-domain context dependency. It proposes DACCA, a framework with cross-domain contrastive loss and domain-level feature aggregation. The introduction motivates the method by describing drawbacks of pixel-wise cross-entropy and limitations of existing domain-adaptive lane detection methods.

item.text: Lane detection models trained on synthetic or source-domain data degrade when transferred to real target domains.
Pixel-wise cross-entropy is described as insufficient for distinguishing feature representations among different lane categories.
Existing domain-adaptive lane detection methods are described as underusing cross-domain context dependency.
DACCA uses positive sample memory modules to store domain-level lane features in source and target domains.
Cross-domain contrastive loss and domain-level feature aggregation are claimed to improve discriminative features and cross-domain knowledge transfer.
The abstract reports 92.24% accuracy on TuLane using RTFormer.

section.title: Related Work
section.summary: This section reviews lane detection, unsupervised domain adaptation, unsupervised domain adaptive lane detection, and context aggregation. It positions the paper relative to segmentation-based lane detection, self-training and adversarial UDA, prototype or contrastive UDA methods, and context aggregation methods.

item.text: The paper focuses on segmentation-based domain-adaptive lane detection.
Discussed related UDA methods include DANN, ADDA, SGADA, SGPCS, Advent, PyCDA, Maximum Squares, and MLDA.
Discussed contrastive or prototype UDA methods include CDCL, ProCA, CONFETI, and SePiCo.
The paper states that methods using pseudo-labels as positives may suffer from false positive sample assignments in the unlabeled target domain.
The paper contrasts DACCA with methods that aggregate context only within a single image or mini-batch.

section.title: Method Overview and Self-Training
section.summary: The method uses a self-training pipeline with a student model and a teacher model. The teacher generates pseudo-labels for target images, low-confidence pseudo-labels are filtered, and the teacher is updated by exponential moving average from the student.

item.text: DACCA trains a student model on labeled source images and unlabeled target images with teacher-generated pseudo-labels.
Source-domain training uses pixel-wise cross-entropy loss.
Teacher pseudo-labels are generated by argmax prediction and filtered by confidence threshold alpha_c.
Target-domain training uses pixel-wise cross-entropy with filtered pseudo-labels.
The teacher is updated from the student by EMA with beta set to 0.9.

section.title: Cross-Domain Contrastive Loss
section.summary: This section introduces a category-wise contrastive loss adapted for cross-domain lane detection. It defines anchor, positive, and negative sample selection policies, including separate source and target positive sample memory modules. The final DACCA objective combines source and target cross-entropy with source and target cross-domain contrastive losses.

item.text: Anchors are selected from lane pixels whose labels or pseudo-labels match class c and whose predicted confidence exceeds threshold mu_c.
Separate source and target PSMMs store domain-level features for each lane as positive samples.
Target-domain negative samples are selected from pixels with the lowest predicted confidence for a category.
Cross-domain contrastive loss consists of inter-domain and intra-domain contrastive learning losses and is applied to source and target domains.
The total training loss combines source CE, target CE, SCCL, and TCCL, with lambda_c set to 0.1.
An extra representation head U produces pixel-wise feature representations during training.

section.title: Domain-Level Feature Aggregation and PSMM Details
section.summary: This section describes domain-level feature aggregation, which assigns source and target domain-level features to pixel locations and fuses them with pixel-level features. It also handles unreliable background pixels and, in the appendix, details PSMM initialization and EMA updates.

item.text: DFA contains source and target domain-level feature assignment modules that fuse domain-level features into pixel-level representations.
Predicted pixel categories are obtained with a 1x1 convolution and softmax, then used to assign PSMM features to a domain-level feature map.
Unreliable background pixels are defined as background predictions with confidence below epsilon.
Unreliable background pixels are assigned pseudo categories by nearest domain-level feature in Euclidean distance.
Pixel-level features, source-assigned features, and target-assigned features are concatenated and fused by 1x1 convolution.
PSMM features are initialized from the center of selected anchor features and updated by EMA with polynomial annealing.

section.title: Experiments and Main Results
section.summary: The experiments evaluate DACCA through component ablations, generalizability across detection models, comparisons with contrastive loss variants and context aggregation methods, and state-of-the-art comparisons. Main reported datasets include TuLane, OpenLane to CULane, and CULane to Tusimple in the main paper.

item.text: Critical component ablation adds SCCL, self-training, TCCL, DFA, and UBP feature aggregation to a source-only SCNN baseline.
SCNN source-only accuracy on TuLane is 77.42%, while full DACCA reaches 83.99% with FP 42.27% and FN 40.10%.
DACCA improves SCNN, ERFNet, and RTFormer source-only baselines; RTFormer+DACCA reaches 92.24% accuracy on TuLane.
TuLane comparisons include DANN, ADDA, SGADA, SGPCS, LD-BN-ADAPT, MLDA, PyCDA, Cross-domain, and Maximum Squares.
On OpenLane to CULane, DACCA reports total score 43.0 versus MLDA 38.8.
On CULane to Tusimple, DACCA reports 92.1% accuracy, FP 26.7%, and FN 14.6%.

section.title: Appendix: Experimental Settings, Hyperparameters, and Additional Experiments
section.summary: The appendix provides dataset descriptions, metrics, implementation details, PSMM details, additional hyperparameter ablations, visualizations, and extra experimental results. It reports experiments on six datasets and additional domain transfer settings.

item.text: Experiments use TuLane, MoLane, MuLane, CULane, Tusimple, and OpenLane.
TuLane, MuLane, MoLane, and Tusimple are evaluated with Accuracy, FP, and FN; CULane and OpenLane use F1 score.
Implementation uses AdamW with initial learning rate 0.0001, Poly learning rate policy, image size 384x800, and a single Tesla V100 GPU.
Hyperparameter studies cover number of anchors M, number of negatives N, anchor threshold mu_c, UBP threshold epsilon, pseudo-label threshold alpha_c, and feature fusion method.
Additional results report DACCA accuracy of 93.50% on MoLane and 90.14% on MuLane using RTFormer.
Additional transfer results include Tusimple to CULane total 41.9 and CULane to OpenLane all-category F1 27.6.

section.title: Conclusion
section.summary: The conclusion restates DACCA as an unsupervised domain-adaptive lane detection method using PSMM, cross-domain contrastive loss, and domain-level feature aggregation. It reports strong performance on TuLane, MuLane, and MoLane relative to existing unsupervised domain-adaptive segmentation-based lane detection methods. The authors state future work on applying DACCA beyond segmentation-based lane detection.

item.text: DACCA is claimed to exploit discriminative feature learning and cross-domain knowledge transfer for lane detection.
PSMM preserves domain-level lane features for use in contrastive learning and aggregation.
The conclusion states that DACCA achieves best performance on TuLane and outperforms existing UDA segmentation-based lane detection methods on MuLane and MoLane.
The paper states DACCA is implemented upon segmentation-based lane detection.
Future work is to explore applying the approach to other lane detection methods such as keypoint-based and transformer-based approaches.

claims.item: DACCA improves discriminative lane feature learning and cross-domain knowledge transfer through contextual contrast and aggregation.
Cross-domain contrastive loss avoids false positive sample assignment by using domain-level features as positives.
Domain-level feature aggregation is claimed to strengthen cross-domain context dependency by fusing source and target domain-level features with pixel-level features.
The paper claims DACCA achieves best performance on TuLane and outperforms existing UDA segmentation-based lane detection methods on MuLane and MoLane.

method_components.item: Student-teacher self-training with filtered pseudo-labels and EMA teacher update.
Cross-domain contrastive loss with anchor, positive, and negative sample selection policies.
Source and target positive sample memory modules storing per-lane domain-level features.
Domain-level feature aggregation using source feature assignment, target feature assignment, concatenation, and 1x1 convolution.
Unreliable background pixel refinement by confidence threshold and nearest domain-level feature assignment.
PSMM initialization from anchor feature centers and EMA update with polynomial annealing.

datasets.item: TuLane: source domain uses 24,000 labeled simulated images; target domain derives from Tusimple.
MoLane: source domain uses 80,000 labeled simulated images; target domain has 43,843 unlabeled real-scene images.
MuLane: combines TuLane and MoLane data, with 48,000 labeled simulated source images and target domains from Tusimple and MoLane.
CULane, Tusimple, and OpenLane are used for additional domain adaptation experiments.
Main transfer settings include OpenLane to CULane and CULane to Tusimple.
Additional transfer settings include Tusimple to CULane and CULane to OpenLane.

baselines.item: Source-only segmentation lane detectors: SCNN, ERFNet, and RTFormer.
Domain adaptive lane detection baselines: DANN, ADDA, SGADA, SGPCS, LD-BN-ADAPT, and MLDA.
Domain adaptive segmentation baselines adapted to lane detection: Advent, PyCDA, Cross-domain, and Maximum Squares.
Contrastive loss variant comparisons: CDCL, ProCA, CONFETI, and SePiCo.
Context aggregation comparisons: Cross-domain and Self-attention module.

ablations.item: Critical component ablation evaluates source-only, SCCL, self-training, TCCL, DFA, and UBP feature aggregation.
Generalizability ablation integrates DACCA with SCNN, ERFNet, and RTFormer.
Contrastive comparison replaces CCL with CDCL, ProCA, CONFETI, and SePiCo.
Context aggregation comparison replaces DFA with Cross-domain and SAM modules.
Hyperparameter ablations study M, N, mu_c, epsilon, alpha_c, and feature fusion method.
Feature fusion ablation compares add, weighted add, and concatenation.

metrics.item: Accuracy is used for TuLane, MuLane, MoLane, and Tusimple lane detection evaluation.
False positives and false negatives are reported as FP and FN rates.
CULane and OpenLane use F1 score for evaluation.
Cosine similarity and temperature tau are used in the category-wise contrastive loss.

results.item: Table 1: full DACCA with SCNN reaches 83.99% accuracy on TuLane versus 77.42% for source-only.
Table 2: RTFormer+DACCA reaches 92.24% accuracy, FP 15.10%, and FN 12.58% on TuLane.
Table 3: DACCA with ERFNet reaches 90.47% accuracy on TuLane; DACCA with RTFormer reaches 92.24%.
Table 4: OpenLane to CULane total score is 43.0 for DACCA.
Table 5: CULane to Tusimple accuracy is 92.1% for DACCA.
Tables A7-A8: DACCA with RTFormer reports 93.50% accuracy on MoLane and 90.14% accuracy on MuLane.

stated_limitations.item: DACCA is implemented upon segmentation-based lane detection.
Future work is to explore use with other lane detection methods, including keypoint-based and transformer-based approaches.
